description_html:
The Wildfire-Aware Optimal Transmission Switching with Undergrounding (WF_OTS_UG) problem extends WF_OTS from operational decisions to long-term planning. Over a horizon of several days, it decides which transmission lines to de-energize on each day and which lines to underground. Undergrounding is a one-time investment, limited by an overall budget, that removes a line's wildfire ignition risk while letting it stay in service. On each day, lines in the highest-risk category must be either de-energized or undergrounded. The remaining (residual) wildfire risk of energized overhead lines must stay below a system-wide threshold. The objective is to minimize total load shedding over the planning horizon. [Pollack25] also studies equity-aware variants, which minimize the maximum share of load shed experienced by any demographic group or require that a specified fraction of the investment or of the load-shed reduction benefits vulnerable communities. The instances in this library use the baseline variant, which minimizes total load shed with no equity objective or policy constraint. Like WF_OTS, WF_OTS_UG is a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) under the DC (Bθ) power flow approximation, with binary variables for daily line energization and for undergrounding. The undergrounding decisions are made once and apply to every day, so they couple the daily switching problems. The result is a larger and harder MILP that trades long-term infrastructure investment against short-term operational shutoffs.

The MILP formulation for the WF_OTS_UG instances in this library is the baseline model (BL) of [Pollack25] (Section 3; Appendix B.6.1 in the journal version). Each day is represented by one operating hour. The Small network is the 240-bus reduced WECC model (pglib_opf_case240_pserc: 240 buses, 448 branches, 143 generators). The Large network is the synthetic Texas7k grid (6,717 buses, 9,140 branches, 637 generators in the instances). Line risks are integrated high-risk USGS WFPI values, which appear in the instances scaled by \(10^{-6}\). The instances of one distribution share the network, days and risks. They differ in per-bus loads (by up to about ±10% between instances) and in the undergrounding budget \(B\) (for the Large network, \(B\in\{0,100,200,300,400,500\}\); with \(B=0\) no line can be undergrounded).

Notation

  • \(\mathcal{D}\): set of days (one operating hour per day); \(\mathcal{N},\mathcal{G},\mathcal{L}\): buses, generators and branches; \(\mathcal{G}_n\), \(\mathcal{L}_n^{fr}\), \(\mathcal{L}_n^{to}\), \(n_\ell^{fr}\), \(n_\ell^{to}\), \(n^{\mathrm{ref}}\): as in WF_OTS.
  • \(r_{\ell,d}\ge 0\): wildfire risk of line \(\ell\) on day \(d\).
  • \(\mathcal{L}^{high}_d=\{\ell: r_{\ell,d}\ge R^{high}\}\) and \(\mathcal{L}^{med}_d=\{\ell: r^{low}\le r_{\ell,d}<R^{high}\}\), with \(R^{high}=1\) in the instances' scaled units and a small cutoff \(r^{low}\) (about \(10^{-4}\)). Lines with \(0<r_{\ell,d}<r^{low}\) cannot be switched (\(z_{\ell,d}\equiv 1\)), but their risk still counts in the daily risk budget. \(\mathcal{L}^{s}_d=\mathcal{L}^{high}_d\cup\mathcal{L}^{med}_d\) are the lines that can be switched on day \(d\).
  • \(\mathcal{L}^{H}=\bigcup_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\): candidate lines for undergrounding.
  • \(d_{n,d}\): demand at bus \(n\) on day \(d\); \(\overline{p}_i\): generator capacity (lower bound 0); \(\overline{f}_\ell\): branch rating; \(b_\ell=x_\ell/(r_\ell^2+x_\ell^2)\): series susceptance, with its sign (negative for the 12 series-compensated branches of the Small network, which have \(x_\ell<0\); positive otherwise).
  • \(\overline{\delta}\): angle-difference limit (\(\pi/6\) for the Small network, \(\pi/3\) for the Large network); \(M=2\pi\).
  • \(\phi_\ell\): cost of undergrounding line \(\ell\) (USD million, at USD 7 million per mile); \(B\): undergrounding budget.
  • \(R^{\mathrm{PSPS}}\): daily risk threshold (\(6\times10^{8}\) unscaled, 600 in the instances).

Variables

  • \(y_\ell\in\{0,1\}\), \(\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{H}\): 1 if line \(\ell\) is undergrounded.
  • \(z_{\ell,d}\in\{0,1\}\), \(\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\), \(d\in\mathcal{D}\): 1 if line \(\ell\) is energized on day \(d\). For \(\ell\notin\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\), \(z_{\ell,d}\equiv1\).
  • \(p_{i,d}\), \(f_{\ell,d}\in[-\overline{f}_\ell,\overline{f}_\ell]\), \(\theta_{n,d}\in[-\pi,\pi]\), \(s_{n,d}\ge0\): generation, flow, voltage angle and load shed on day \(d\).

MILP formulation

\begin{align} \min\quad & \sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\sum_{n\in\mathcal{N}} s_{n,d} \\ \text{s.t.}\quad & 0\le p_{i,d}\le \overline{p}_i, && \forall i\in\mathcal{G},d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & 0\le s_{n,d}\le d_{n,d}, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N},d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & -\overline{f}_\ell z_{\ell,d}\le f_{\ell,d}\le \overline{f}_\ell z_{\ell,d}, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\\ & -\overline{\delta}-M(1-z_{\ell,d})\le \theta_{n_\ell^{fr},d}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to},d}\le \overline{\delta}+M(1-z_{\ell,d}), && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\\ & -|b_\ell| M(1-z_{\ell,d})\le f_{\ell,d}-b_\ell(\theta_{n_\ell^{fr},d}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to},d})\le |b_\ell| M(1-z_{\ell,d}), && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\\ & -\overline{\delta}\le \theta_{n_\ell^{fr},d}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to},d}\le \overline{\delta}, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\\ & f_{\ell,d}=b_\ell(\theta_{n_\ell^{fr},d}-\theta_{n_\ell^{to},d}), && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}\setminus\mathcal{L}^{s}_d\\ & \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}_n^{fr}} f_{\ell,d}-\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}_n^{to}} f_{\ell,d}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{G}_n} p_{i,d}-d_{n,d}+s_{n,d}, && \forall n\in\mathcal{N},d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & \theta_{n^{\mathrm{ref}},d}=0, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & z_{\ell,d}=y_\ell, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{high}_d\\ & y_\ell\le z_{\ell,d}, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{med}_d\\ & \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}} r_{\ell,d}\,(z_{\ell,d}-y_\ell)\le R^{\mathrm{PSPS}}, && \forall d\in\mathcal{D}\\ & \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{H}} \phi_\ell\, y_\ell\le B\\ & y_\ell\in\{0,1\},\ \forall \ell\in\mathcal{L}^{H};\quad z_{\ell,d}\in\{0,1\},\ \forall d\in\mathcal{D},\ell\in\mathcal{L}^{s}_d \end{align}

Each daily block is the DC optimal transmission switching model of WF_OTS ([Pollack25] Eq. (1)) with its own copy of the operating variables. The undergrounding variables \(y_\ell\) link the days. A high-risk line must be either undergrounded or de-energized (\(z=y\)). A medium-risk line cannot be both undergrounded and de-energized (\(y\le z\), i.e., \((1-z)+y\le1\)). The daily risk budget counts only energized overhead lines (in the sum, \(y_\ell\equiv0\) for \(\ell\notin\mathcal{L}^{H}\), and constant terms are moved to the right-hand side). The undergrounding budget limits total investment. The objective is the total load shed. It is equivalent to the fraction of load shed \(S\) used in [Pollack25], because total demand is a constant. The instance files also contain an unused auxiliary variable aux_max \(\ge0\), left over from the equity (min-max) variants, with objective coefficient 0. Each instance has \(|\mathcal{L}^{H}|+\sum_d|\mathcal{L}^{s}_d|\) binary variables, \(|\mathcal{D}|(2|\mathcal{N}|+|\mathcal{L}|+|\mathcal{G}|)+1\) continuous variables and \(\sum_d\big(3|\mathcal{N}|+3|\mathcal{L}|+4|\mathcal{L}^{s}_d|+2\big)+2\) constraints (the load-shed bounds are written as rows).
changes: Citation key [Pollack24] changed to [Pollack25]: Pollack, Piansky, Gupta, Molzahn, 'Equitably allocating wildfire resilience investments for power grids - the curse of aggregation and vulnerability indices', Applied Energy 388 (2025) 125511; arXiv:2404.11520. In the arXiv v4 the formulation is in Section 3 (Eqs. (1)-(7), model BL); 'Appendix B.6.1' presumably refers to the journal version and could not be checked.

Prose: states that the instances use the baseline (min total load shed) variant, not an equity variant; the instance objective has coefficient 1 on every load-shed variable, and aux_max (the equity alpha) has objective 0 and only the row aux_max >= 0. The prose now says that one operating hour represents each day and names the test systems.
Added notation, variables, the complete MILP and count formulas.

Identified the networks. Small = 240-bus reduced WECC model (Price & Goodin 2011; pglib_opf_case240_pserc), matched on 240 buses, 448 branches, 143 generators, bus IDs 1001-8034 and +-30 deg angle limits. Large = Texas7k synthetic grid (TAMU; named in [Pollack25] Section 4.1), matched on 6,717 buses and 9,140 branches (637 generators appear in the instances). Possible new reference: Price, J. E., & Goodin, J. (2011), 'Reduced network modeling of WECC as a market design prototype', IEEE PES General Meeting.
Network size and Number of days (16, 31, 1, 2) are confirmed correct. Added columns Test system, # Buses and # Branches.
verification: Fetched easy rows 0 and 1, medium rows 0 and 1, hard rows 0 and 1, and hard2 row 0, and parsed them with highspy.

Days are counted from the variable index (day, hour, id): easy 16, medium 31, hard 1, hard2 2, always with hour index 1 only. Per day: Small has 240 theta, 240 s, 448 f and 143 p; Large has 6,717 / 6,717 / 9,140 / 637.

Easy row 0: 4,181 binary (3,881 z + 300 y), 17,137 continuous (incl. aux_max) and 48,582 rows. Hard row 0: 3,982 binary (1,991 z + 1,991 y), 23,212 continuous and 55,539 rows. Hard2 row 0: 6,546 binary (4,164 z + 2,382 y). Medium: 7,525 binary (7,236 z + 289 y), 33,202 continuous and 92,992 rows. All of these match the table and the count formula exactly.

There is one z-y link row per z: equality z = y when r >= 1 (minimum 1.0037), and y - z <= 0 when 0 < r < 1 (maximum 0.9946). This matches R_high = 1e6 scaled by 1e-6. The set of y lines is exactly the union of the daily switchable sets.

There is one risk row per day, with +r on z and -r on y, and RHS 600 (= 6e8 * 1e-6). On one day of easy and of medium, 2 lines with r of about 4.2e-5 have y but no z; their constant is moved to the RHS (599.99991).
Budget row: sum phi_l y_l <= B. Observed B: easy 940 and 950; medium 920 and 940; hard 300 and 300; hard2 400. phi_l ranges from 15.07 to 2,664.35 (Small) and from 0.048 to 820.13 (Large).
Angle big-M rows have RHS delta + 2*pi (6.80678 for Small = pi/6 + 2*pi, 7.33039 for Large = pi/3 + 2*pi). The flow big-M equals 2*pi*b_l. Theta bounds are [-pi, pi]; generator lower bounds are 0.

Two instances of the same distribution have identical generator bounds, risks and phi. Per-bus loads differ by a ratio of 0.905-1.103 (consistent with independent perturbations of about +-5% each; this is inferred, not confirmed).
open_questions: How instances were generated (load perturbation range, how B is sampled, which days and hour were chosen) was inferred from the instances. No generator code was found.
The exact rule for the low-risk set is unclear: on one day, 2 lines with r ~ 4.2e-5 (scaled) are not switchable, yet lines with r as low as 2.5e-4 are.
Appendix B.6.1 of the Applied Energy version could not be accessed; the formulation follows arXiv v4 Section 3 and the instances.
The Texas7k generator count (637 in the instances) was not checked against the source file; the original case may contain more generators, with out-of-service units removed.
